scope: Batch 3 (AI Product Editor and Maintainer), development only. All three phases (Work Packages A to G): existing GitHub repository or ZIP connection, commit-keyed code map, safe AI change execution with isolated real tests, bounded repair, durable revisions and stacked follow-ups, draft-PR delivery and export, the Existing project workspace tab, and certification (Golden A to L, negative matrix). Extends the existing SoftwareAgent tool-host contract, sandbox runtime and atomic GitHub writer; adds no scheduler or runtime. Integration milestone 2026-10-29: main merged; each change now runs as a canonical durable run (same outbox, Cloud Run Job claim, run attempt, cancellation and terminal authority). Commands execute only through the existing canonical sandbox seam, and the run's own attempt-bound execution state holds the exact working files, so no authority is manufactured. Live Google execution is not yet exercised.

keep: Canonical scheduler, SoftwareAgent, repositoryTools session, patch workspace and GitHub persistence
Existing GitHub OAuth connection and its revocation semantics
extend: Existing repositories are bound by GitHub immutable repository id, connected account and exact base commit
Tree reads walk truncated trees directory by directory and report partial honestly
Credential-bearing paths are listed but their content is never fetched

schemaImpact.rollout: Additive service-role-only table with RLS and no public grants. Not applied by this change; apply through the verified migration workflow after authorisation.
schemaImpact.rollback: DROP TABLE public.existing_source_changes; DROP TABLE public.existing_source_archives; DROP TABLE public.existing_source_indexes; DROP TABLE public.existing_source_projects; (the archive migration also relaxes the origin_kind check; nothing else references these tables).

auth.description: New /api/existing-source routes require the issued tenant context and are off unless XROGA_EXISTING_SOURCE=1.

tenant.description: Every binding query carries the verified owner; another owner's binding id is indistinguishable from one that does not exist; the same repository linked by two owners stays two bindings. Code maps are stored per owner and binding, service-role only with RLS, cascade on unlink, purged on revocation, transfer, account change and removed connection; another owner's map is indistinguishable from a missing one.

approval.description: Delivery writes a NEW review branch and opens a draft PR only after the binding is re-verified at the provider, the account can push, the remote head is re-read, credentials and workflow paths are scanned out, and the change is verified (or explicitly confirmed unverified). It never writes the base or a protected branch and never force-pushes. An unverified change needs an explicit acknowledgement before a draft PR.

credentials.description: The connected account token is resolved server-side and never returned; .env, key and credential files are never fetched; secrets inside ordinary files are redacted by the existing tool session.

egress.description: Calls only api.github.com with the connected account's own token, addressed by repository id; blob fetches for the map skip sensitive, vendored, generated, binary and oversize files. No repository content reaches a model in these phases; the passport carries signatures and paths, not bodies. A ZIP import is read only from the owner's own upload; entries are validated (no traversal, symlink, encrypted, bomb), and credentials and binaries are never stored. Change execution and tests run only through the isolation runtime port (never on the API host); with no runtime the change ends unverified.

cost.description: Map builds are bounded (1500 blob fetches, 24 MB, one build at a time per owner, shared in-flight builds); persisted map capped at 8 MB. No model spend.

tests.scope: Link, tenant isolation, revocation, exact-commit reads, and the code map routes over HTTP
Language adapters, graph, ground-truth relevance on a 638-file monorepo, reuse, incremental equals cold build, stale never served, overlay, limits, concurrency, Python and Go
Every client call is a served route with the same method; the screen reports partial maps and builds only on request
Migration registration and tenant audit register
Hostile ZIP handling, import, link, read, map, tenant isolation, unlink cleanup

Real Node and Python test runs, reproduction check, bounded repair, honest statuses, cancellation and recovery, injection and abuse, tenant isolation, draft PR delivery, divergence, idempotency, export
Golden A to L and the negative matrix: real node and python runs, honest not-run labels, conflict and rebase, injection obedience, recovery, outages
Change screen rules and rendering: honest statuses, escaped diff, delivery gating, unverified acknowledgement, conflict display

Canonical port keeps the run state in step with the working files, picks the right sandbox caller, refuses another attempt or owner and ignores a supplied binding; the Job refuses a change not queued for its run and records cancellation; the queued change id is validated; launching queues a canonical run or ends the change with a reason. All PASS with fakes; no live Google run.

architecture.reason: Adds a binding store and a read-only source service around the existing RepositoryToolSession. No scheduler, agent loop, runtime or authentication system is added.

rollout: Development only. Merge, migration and activation need the founder's explicit authorisation after all six phases and acceptance gates.
rollback: Leave XROGA_EXISTING_SOURCE and NEXT_PUBLIC_XROGA_EXISTING_SOURCE unset: routes answer 503 and the page is absent. Drop the table with the statement above if the migration was applied.
knownGaps: No live GitHub verification (needs an authorised disposable account)
No real model (Cline) run: no provider spend was authorised
Google isolated execution not connected: it needs a canonical run attempt per change, so changes there end unverified
Go tests not executed (no toolchain here); Preview and browser verification not connected; Golden E blocked, Golden H not run
UI verified by render and contract tests only, not in a live browser or with assistive technology
Stores have no real-database test; no retention policy for old changes
Canonical execution is verified with fakes only; a live Cloud Run Job and Google sandbox run of a change has not been done
placeholderClaimsRemaining: Live provider behaviour is unverified; only a faithful in-memory GitHub was exercised
